messages:
alex: heads-up — p99 on prod inference jumped from ~210ms to ~560ms after the 1824987 runtime push. SLO is 400ms. I'm starting a quick root-cause thread, tagging @maya @sam.

maya: saw the alert. initial flamegraphs point to a small set of requests dominating tail. seems related to: long user prompts + tool-calling chatter + microbatch growth. :thinking:

sam: concrete numbers: p50 ~ 120ms, p95 ~ 260ms (ok), p99 ~ 560ms. throughput unchanged. CPU on host is fine, GPU util steady. traces show huge time inside kernel launch + memcpy for some shards.

jess: i grabbed profiler: attached snippet of wall times (top ops):
```
op: matmul_v2         count: 1123   median: 1.2ms   p99: 48ms
op: kv_cache_lookup   count: 2345   median: 0.2ms   p99: 22ms
op: dispatch_kernel   count: 1123   median: 0.1ms   p99: 120ms
```
Notice dispatch_kernel p99 is big.

pranav: that dispatch_kernel p99 spike smells like kernel selection flip-flopping for same model shapes. iirc we changed kernel-pref logic in last deploy to prefer the "cuda_matmul_agg" path for sm86. Could be a mismatch for quantized kernels.

maya: matching this to request characteristics — most long-tail requests have: (a) >1200 tokens prompt, (b) tool-call loop (we append tool output as structured JSON each step), which pushes effective seq_len to >1500 mid-gen, and (c) cold KV cache (no prefix reuse).

alex: so three axes: long seq_len, tool loop causing repeated KV expansion, and kernel pick that maybe isn’t optimal for big seq_len+quant. Any quick experiment ideas?

sam: try 2 quick things: 1) force kernel fallback to the older matmul path for seq_len > 1024, 2) reduce microbatch window from 250ms -> 50ms for one canary host to see p99 impact.

jess: ran (1) on a canary box — dispatch_kernel p99 drops from 120ms -> 28ms for those requests. overall p99 drops ~120ms. but throughput on the canary dropped ~10% due to less parallelism.

pranav: ran (2) — reduced batch window to 50ms on a different canary: p99 improved ~80ms, but throughput dropped ~12% and CPU jitter increased. cost per token up ~8% in our sim.

alex: so tradeoff confirmed: tighter microbatch window lowers tail but costs throughput. kernel fallback fixes latency without as much throughput loss but may regress overall throughput for small-seq workloads.

maya: another angle: KV-cache prewarm for long prompts/tool loops. If we detect tool-call intent (heuristics: JSON markers, repeated tool ids), prewarm KV and pin small batch size for that request. Cheap to try: add rule to route to a conservative path with warmup.

sam: good. also we found a regression: commit 7b3c22 changed kernel heuristics to use estimated FLOPs rather than measured wall-time; for quantized matmuls the FLOP estimate is misleading — selects a kernel with bad memory pattern for our quant layout. revert or special-case quantized models.

jess: stack trace/log for one slow request:
```
[trace] request_id=abc123
seq_len_before=620 prompt=1400 tokens (truncated)
kernel_choice=cuda_matmul_agg (quant)
kv_cache_misses=48
batch_size_at_call=14
dispatch_latency=317ms
kernel_exec=230ms
```
Notice kernel_exec >> typical.

maya: action items proposed:
- revert FLOP-based kernel pick for quantized models (pranav)
- add rule: if seq_len_est > 1024 or tool-loop detected => route to conservative kernel + prewarm KV (sam)
- experiment: adaptive microbatch cap per-request (limit microbatch to 4 for flagged requests) (jess)
- telemetry: add counters for kernel-flip events and avg kernel_exec by quant flag (alex)

alex: agreed. prioritization: revert heuristic first (fast rollback). then telemetry. then conservative routing + prewarm. microbatch cap is last since it impacts throughput.

deploy-bot: canary rollback initiated for runtime-kernel-heuristic @ 1825000045 by pranav.

pranav: rollback confirmed on 2 canaries. early metrics: canary p99 down ~90ms. leaving rollback until we add quant special-case tests.

sam: once rollback is in, i'll push KV prewarm rule as a config flag so we can opt-in. need to be careful with memory pressure (prewarming adds KV occupancy).

jess: note for postmortem: some customer logs show tool loops generating deep JSON arrays that expand tokenization unpredictably — need a guard to truncate or promote to streaming tool output rather than re-embedding whole JSON each step.

alex: thanks all. next steps tracker: pranav rollback ✅, alex add telemetry dashboard, sam add config flag for prewarm, jess prototype adaptive microbatch cap. we'll reconvene in 2 hours with updated canary numbers. :eyes:

maya: also quick note — add an eval that simulates long prompt + tool-loop to our perf harness. current perf tests don't exercise this pattern.

alex: good call. I'll assign.

sam: tagging this for follow-up in eng-runtime sync. short doc + bullet summary to come.
